Session players get hired for their ears more than their hands. Mine are decent on intervals and bad on chord qualities, which is embarrassing at 45.

## Intervals

Using the app Tonedear, 15 minutes after breakfast. Scores from April 2025: ascending intervals 94%, descending 81%, harmonic (both notes at once) 72%. The minor 6th versus major 6th descending is still a coin toss.

Reference songs I use, because everyone does:

- Minor 2nd down: "Für Elise" opening
- Tritone: "The Simpsons" theme
- Major 6th up: "My Bonnie Lies over the Ocean", fitting for a Glaswegian

## Chord qualities

Big weakness. Can't reliably tell m7b5 from dim7 in a dense voicing. Drill: Fergus plays a chord on the Nord, I name it, 20 chords a round. Best score so far 16/20 (2 May 2025).

## Transcription

Rhythm first, then bass line, then top line, then the middle. Two bars a day of something hard rather than a page of something easy. Current: the piano intro to Bill Evans "Peace Piece" (1958).

## Spacing it out

I put the intervals I fail into a flashcard deck and let the app bring them back on a growing gap, borrowed straight from [[Spaced repetition intervals]]. Singing back what I hear works like the [[Shadowing technique]] for languages: hear it, sing it, then check it on the guitar. Related: [[Guitar practice]], [[Music theory modes]].
